questions.enonce_markdown: Find the distances from $PS$ and $PQ$ of the centre of mass of the lamina.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Geometry.** In the figure $PSRT$ is a rectangle ($PS$ and $TR$ vertical, $PT = SR = 5a$) and $T$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $R$ to $PQ$. [The height $RT$ is not labelled in the figure: its value and the right angle at $T$ are deduced here from the drawing.] In the right-angled triangle $RTQ$:

$$RT^2 = RQ^2 - TQ^2 = 25a^2 - 9a^2 = 16a^2\;\Longrightarrow\; RT = 4a$$

so $PS = RT = 4a$ and $PQ = PT + TQ = 8a$. The lamina is split into the rectangle $PSRT$ ($5a\times 4a$) and the right-angled triangle $RTQ$ (base $TQ = 3a$, height $RT = 4a$).

**Axes.** Origin $P$; $x$-axis along $PQ$ (so $x$ is the distance from $PS$); $y$-axis along $PS$ (so $y$ is the distance from $PQ$). The lamina is uniform, so the mass of each part is proportional to its area (the surface density cancels) and the centre of mass is the centroid.

| Part | Area | $x$ (distance from $PS$) | $y$ (distance from $PQ$) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rectangle $PSRT$ | $5a\times 4a = 20a^2$ | $\tfrac52 a$ | $2a$ |
| Triangle $RTQ$ | $\tfrac12\times 3a\times 4a = 6a^2$ | $5a + \tfrac13(3a) = 6a$ | $\tfrac13(4a) = \tfrac43 a$ |
| Whole lamina | $26a^2$ | $\bar x$ | $\bar y$ |

(The centroid of a right-angled triangle lies one third of the way along each leg from the right-angle vertex $T$. Check of the total area with the trapezium formula: $\tfrac12(5a + 8a)(4a) = 26a^2$.)

**Moments about $PS$:**

$$26a^2\,\bar x = 20a^2\left(\tfrac52 a\right) + 6a^2(6a) = 50a^3 + 36a^3 = 86a^3\;\Longrightarrow\;\bar x = \frac{43a}{13}\approx 3.31a$$

**Moments about $PQ$:**

$$26a^2\,\bar y = 20a^2(2a) + 6a^2\left(\tfrac43 a\right) = 40a^3 + 8a^3 = 48a^3\;\Longrightarrow\;\bar y = \frac{24a}{13}\approx 1.85a$$

**The centre of mass is at distance $\dfrac{43a}{13}$ from $PS$ and $\dfrac{24a}{13}$ from $PQ$.**
themes: centre of mass of composite bodies

questions.enonce_markdown: If the lamina is freely suspended from $S$, calculate the tangent of the angle the edge $PS$ makes with the vertical.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Suspended freely from $S$, the lamina is in equilibrium under its weight (acting at the centre of mass $G$) and the reaction at $S$. These two forces are equal and opposite, so $G$ lies **vertically below $S$**: the line $SG$ is vertical.

In the axes of part (a), $S = (0, 4a)$ and $G = \left(\dfrac{43a}{13},\ \dfrac{24a}{13}\right)$. The edge $SP$ runs from $S$ straight down the line $x = 0$. Consider the right-angled triangle formed by $S$, $G$ and the foot of the perpendicular from $G$ to $SP$ (the point at height $\dfrac{24a}{13}$ on $PS$):

- opposite side (horizontal distance of $G$ from $PS$) $= \dfrac{43a}{13}$,
- adjacent side (distance along $SP$ from $S$ down to the level of $G$) $= 4a - \dfrac{24a}{13} = \dfrac{28a}{13}$.

If $\theta$ is the angle between $PS$ and the vertical $SG$:

$$\tan\theta = \frac{43a/13}{28a/13} = \frac{43}{28}\approx 1.54\qquad(\theta\approx 56.9^\circ)$$

**$\tan\theta = \dfrac{43}{28}$.**
themes: equilibrium of a suspended lamina mechanics
